ConnectionStrings.//Database: Connects as gymos_app, matching docker-compose.override.yml's own string for the api service, so a host-run `dotnet run` against the local sidecar exercises the same non-owner principal the Docker deployment does — never sa, which holds ALTER ANY SECURITY POLICY and which TenantIsolationValidator refuses to boot on. `localhost,1433` rather than `mssql,1433` because the host reaches the sidecar over the published port instead of the compose network; set MSSQL_PORT in .env and change it here to match if 1433 is taken. TrustServerCertificate=True in development and nowhere else: the sidecar generates a self-signed certificate on first boot, so verification cannot succeed against it. `db-init` has to have run at least once, or neither this database nor this login exists — `docker compose up -d db-init` is enough.

Jwt.//SigningKey: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY — this value is public, in version control, and identical for every developer. It is loaded only when ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development, exactly like the dev database password above. Every other environment must supply its own via environment or Key Vault; startup fails when it is missing.

//Seed: The initial SuperAdmin is deliberately NOT configured here — a committed credential would ship identically to every checkout. Create one with: dotnet user-secrets set "Seed:SuperAdmin:Email" "you@example.com" && dotnet user-secrets set "Seed:SuperAdmin:Password" "<a long unique password>" (project src/Host/GymOS.WebApi). Until then the seeder logs a warning and does nothing.
